note: Synthetic claims for the recall eval: a made-up person, never the owner's data. The store is shaped like a real workspace after a few months: one-line preferences, page-long operational notes an agent wrote, pins from other projects and one-off events. Each case is a message, the chat's project, the claim keys a turn must be given and the ones it must not.

Triage note: when a scheduled job fails with 'notify: the discord surface is not connected', the job definition is fine. The host restarted and the job fired before the Discord adapter reconnected. Re-run the job once the surface is up; do not edit the job, its schedule or its actions. Seen on job 4 and job 9 after restarts in October; both ran clean on the retry. If it fails again after the surface is connected, then read the run log for the real error before changing anything about the job or the project it belongs to.

Job 4, first created as 'Morning Test' to test that scheduling works, is now the daily 08:00 kickoff: it runs every day, reads the reading, budget and workout projects, and posts a summary to the Discord channel. The test name stayed in its history; the job itself is the kickoff now, enabled, task cheap. Changing its schedule or project list goes through the Schedule page, and a test run is the run button, which posts for real.

Re-verified: the Discord channel tools exist on this install (discord.server, discord.channel, discord.thread). An earlier note said they were absent; that was before the adapter update. Use discord.server to list categories and channels, discord.thread to list a channel's threads, and notify with to: discord:channel:<id> to post. A test post goes to the channel for real, so test in the private test channel, not the public one, and say what the test was for.

Between two nightly backups in October the workspace lost the reading, budget, workout and garden projects' tables at once; the run log showed a failed job and a test restore. They were restored from the earlier snapshot the same day. Since then the backup job runs a test restore weekly. If a project looks empty, check the snapshot list first and run nothing that writes to the project until it is known whether it is a restore or a real deletion.

Script skills here are Node ESM, not Python: skills.create writes the content to skills/<name>/run.mjs and runs it with node. A test run of a skill goes through skills.run with sample input. A project's scripts live in its own folder and are not skills; a job can run either, but only a skill shows on the Skills page.
